**10 års planen** (The 10-Year Plan) is a Danish political strategy designed to improve care and outcomes for individuals with ADHD. It serves as a critical political initiative aimed at reversing negative trends in ADHD treatment by driving increased resource allocation and fostering cross-systemic collaboration [^src1]. 

The plan is prominently featured in discussions surrounding the systemic crises within Danish psychiatric care. According to quality indicators reported by [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]], the healthcare system is currently struggling to meet baseline standards for ADHD assessment and treatment, with process indicators falling far below the required 90% threshold. In this context, the political momentum generated by "10 års planen"—working in tandem with the massive efforts of the DMPGer (multidisciplinary psychiatric groups)—provides a necessary sense of hope that these negative developments can be overturned [^src1].

Beyond high-level political focus, the strategy is tied to specific clinical improvements. There is a strong expectation that the 10-Year Plan will channel increased resources directly into the psychiatric sector, which is essential for the (re)establishment of psychoeducational offerings for patients [^src2]. This is a crucial development, as current systemic weaknesses have severely hindered cross-sectoral coordination and delayed vital treatments like psychoeducation. Ultimately, "10 års planen" represents a foundational political mobilization intended to address structural resource shortages and improve the overall quality of psychiatric care.
